remaining_nodes.text: Dextran: pronounced anticoagulant effects, impairs platelet function, reduces vWF/FVIII, impairs fibrin polymerization, associated with increased blood loss
HES: effects dependent on MW, C2/C6, DS. High MW/slowly degradable = more impairment. Low MW/rapidly degradable = fewer effects.
Gelatin: least adverse effect on coagulation among synthetic colloids
MW/substitution mechanism: all synthetic colloids decrease vWF/FVIII:C; degree correlates with MW and elimination rate; rapidly degradable = fewest effects
Gelatin vs HES comparison: gelatin shows fewer hemostatic effects than slowly degradable HES, comparable to rapidly degradable HES
Blood coagulation most impaired by dextran and high MW/slowly degradable HES, associated with increased blood loss
The most important determinant of hemostatic safety of plasma substitutes is the rate of degradation.
remaining_nodes.detail: Depends on C1N5 (MW/degradation mechanism) and C1N9 (dextran/slowly-degradable worst). Both clean, both present after pruning.

remaining_nodes.text: In patients with increased risk of bleeding, rapidly degradable HES 200/0.5/6 may be preferred over slowly degradable HES or dextran.
remaining_nodes.detail: Depends on C1N7 (deleted — contaminated by Boldt 1996) and C1N9 (clean but only says dextran/slowly-degradable worst, cannot independently support HES 200/0.5/6 safety). No clean support path remains.

remaining_nodes.text: In patients with increased risk of bleeding, gelatin-based plasma expanders may be preferred over slowly degradable HES or dextran.
remaining_nodes.detail: Depends on C1N6 (gelatin vs HES comparison, clean) and C1N9 (clean). Both present after pruning.

remaining_nodes.text: The same colloid preferences apply to patients with von Willebrand disease. All artificial colloids could potentially induce increased bleeding tendency after infusion of very large volumes.
remaining_nodes.detail: vWb disease preference inherits mixed status from C1N12 (unsupported) and C1N13 (still_supported). Large volume caveat supported by C1N15 (clean). Human review needed to determine vWb-specific recommendation.
